reason: E2 shows that dropwise synthesis yields solid-solution HEA nanocrystals by controlling precursor delivery, supporting the role of deposition rate. E3 demonstrates that single-phase HEA forms more readily with more elements and can occur under sequential reduction when atom mobility is limited, directly backing the kinetic trapping and dilution premises. E1 describes phase separation under fast reduction of Pd, which the hypothesis acknowledges as a boundary condition (disparate reduction potentials), so it does not contradict the core premises.
premises: Rapid atom deposition can outpace surface diffusion during nucleation
Limited surface diffusion kinetically traps a random atomic configuration
A high number of elements dilutes local concentrations, suppressing preferential bonding or segregation
Sequential reduction can still yield a homogeneous alloy if deposition is fast enough
Dropwise addition increases the instantaneous deposition rate relative to a slower injection baseline
